To proceed, spring up or rise, as a consequence, from facts, arguments, premises, combination of circumstances, consultation, thought or endeavor.

examples.text: Pleasure and peace do naturally result from a holy and good life.

glosses: To have as a consequence; to lead to; to bring about

examples.text: This measure will result in good or in evil.

The defender's only reaction was to haul the Italian down, resulting in an inevitable red card.

glosses: That which results; the conclusion or end to which any course or condition of things leads, or which is obtained by any process or operation; consequence or effect.

In America alone, people spent $170 billion on “direct marketing”—junk mail of both the physical and electronic varieties—last year. And for online adverts the “conversion” into sales was a minuscule 0.01%.

glosses: The final product, beneficial or tangible effect(s) achieved by effort.
